name: turn
title: Turn (amount of turn)
tagline: Amount of turn about a centre (quarter/half/three-quarter/full, clockwise or anticlockwise) as a sweep arrow, turn-dial or landmarks rosette; angle and fraction derived.
description: The amount of turn (a rotation) about a centre, for KS1/KS2 "position and direction": a start heading sweeps to an end heading by a given amount, drawn as a bold curved arrow with the swept fraction of a turn and the angle in degrees read off. Choose a scene: "arrow" (an abstract start pointer, a ghost end pointer and the sweep arrow), "dial" (a turn-dial — a face with a hand turning and a rim arc, the turn cousin of an analogue clock), or "rosette" (a ring of labelled landmarks with a little person at the centre turning to face a new one). The author writes the turn — a fraction ("quarter", "half", "three-quarter", "full", or an a/b form) or degrees — and its direction (clockwise / anticlockwise), or a start and a target heading; the swept angle, the reduced fraction of a turn, the end heading, the sweep arc (the short way or, for three-quarter turns, the reflex way round) and the person's new facing are all derived. A friendly stem sentence ("A quarter turn clockwise"; "Facing the school, turn a quarter turn clockwise to face the park") restates the figure. Occlude the turn amount for "how much is the turn?" or the end for "where do you end up facing?"; on the web, pupils can drag to make the turn, snapping to the scene's natural positions.
whenToUse: Reach for this for amount of turn and position-and-direction (KS1/KS2): quarter / half / three-quarter / whole turns, clockwise vs anticlockwise, fractions of a turn, and "turn to face" landmark problems. Pick a scene: scene "arrow" (default) for the pure amount of turn — a pointer turns and a curved arrow shows the sweep; scene "dial" for fractions of a turn on a face (a single hand turning, the turn version of a clock — set show.numerals true for a clock face, false for a quarter-marked dial); scene "rosette" for "facing the ___, turn ___ to face the ___" — give landmarks, each with an at heading and a label, and reference them by id in start/to. Specify the turn in one of two ways: (1) turn: { fraction: "quarter" } (or "half" / "three-quarter" / "full", or "1/3", "3/4", "5/8") OR turn: { degrees: 90 } PLUS a top-level direction ("clockwise" or "anticlockwise") — the end heading is derived; or (2) to: a target heading (with direction to say which way round) — the fraction and degrees are derived, the natural form for "turn to face the park" and "from 12 to 6". start sets the heading you begin from (default straight up / 12 / north). Watch the hard case: a three-quarter turn clockwise and a quarter turn anticlockwise end the same way but sweep differently — the model draws the correct reflex (long-way-round) arc and honours direction, so always state the direction. show toggles the furniture: degrees / fraction (the two readouts), startPointer / endPointer, arc, marks, person (rosette), numerals & compass. occlude "turn" hides the amount as "?" ("how big is this turn?"); occlude "end" hides where you finish ("after this turn, which way / which landmark do you face?"). Keep stem.show true for the verbal twin in primary; set it false with a caption for an answer space. Keep the same scene, start and direction across one lesson so pupils compare like with like. Switch model when the teaching changes: to rotate a shape about a point on a coordinate grid use geometry/transformations; to tell the time or read the angle between two clock hands use geometry/clock. Synonyms a teacher might use: turn, amount of turn, quarter turn, half turn, three-quarter turn, whole turn, full turn, clockwise, anticlockwise, fraction of a turn, rotate, rotation, right angle, direction, compass, position and direction, face, facing.

oneOf.description: Degrees clockwise from straight up (north / 12 o'clock): 0 = up, 90 = right, 180 = down, 270 = left.

A named heading: a compass point ("N", "NE", "E", "SE", "S", "SW", "W", "NW"); a cardinal word ("up", "down", "left", "right"); a clock hour as a string ("12", "3", "6", "9", … → that hour's position); or the id of one of the landmarks (rosette). Resolved in that order, so give landmarks descriptive ids (park, school), not compass letters.

scene.description: Which backdrop the turn is drawn on. "arrow" (default): an abstract turn — a start pointer, a ghost end pointer and the curved sweep arrow. "dial": a turn-dial — a circular face with one hand turning and a rim arc (set show.numerals for a clock-style face). "rosette": a ring of labelled landmarks with a little person at the centre turning to face a new one. All three share the same turn engine and derived readouts.

start.description: The heading you begin from (default straight up — north / 12 o'clock). A number is degrees clockwise from up; a string is a compass point, cardinal word, clock hour, or — in the rosette scene — a landmark id (the person starts facing that landmark).

direction.description: The sense of the turn. Default "clockwise". With "to" it also decides WHICH WAY ROUND the turn goes (the same start and end give a quarter turn one way or a three-quarter turn the other), so always set it deliberately.

turn.description: The amount of turn (the AUTHORED turn). Give EITHER a fraction OR degrees; the other readout and the end heading are derived. Omit "turn" and give "to" instead to specify the turn by its target heading. With neither, a quarter turn is assumed.

fraction.description: A friendly fraction of a FULL turn: "quarter", "half", "three-quarter", "full" (or "whole"), or an a/b form like "1/4", "1/3", "2/3", "3/4", "1/8", "5/8". Derived: degrees = fraction × 360 (a quarter turn = 90°).

degrees.description: The turn in degrees (e.g. 90, 120, 270) — use for a turn that is not a friendly fraction. Derived: the fraction of a turn = degrees ÷ 360, reduced. If both fraction and degrees are given, fraction wins.

to.description: An alternative to "turn": the TARGET heading to turn TO. The turn amount (fraction and degrees) is then derived from start → to, going round in "direction". The natural form for "turn to face the park" (a landmark id) and "from 12 to 6". If both "turn" and "to" are given, "turn" wins.

landmarks.description: Labelled landmarks placed around the rim — the heart of the rosette scene (also usable as named points on the arrow/dial scenes). Each sits at a bearing "at"; reference one as a heading by its id in "start" / "to".

at.description: The landmark's bearing from the centre (a number of degrees clockwise from up, or a compass / cardinal / clock-hour string).

id.description: Optional kebab-case id for referencing this landmark in "start" / "to". Defaults to a slug of the label.

highlight.description: Amber this landmark — the target the person is turning to face. Default false.

occlude.description: "none" (default) shows everything. "turn" hides the amount of turn (the fraction and degrees) as "?" — the "how big is this turn?" question (the sweep arc still shows). "end" hides where you finish (the end pointer and, on a rosette, which landmark) so pupils work out the end heading from the start and the given turn — "after this turn, which way / which landmark do you face?".

degrees.description: Show the swept angle in degrees ("90°"). Default true.

fraction.description: Show the fraction of a turn ("¼ turn" / "a quarter turn"). Default true.

startPointer.description: Draw the start pointer (the heading you begin from). Default true.

endPointer.description: Draw the end pointer (where you finish). Default true. Forced off by occlude "end".

arc.description: Draw the curved sweep arrow / rim arc showing the turn. Default true.

marks.description: Draw the light tick marks around the rim (the quarter / eighth or clock positions). Default true.

numerals.description: Dial scene: show the 1–12 clock numerals (a clock-style face). Default false (a plain quarter-marked dial).

compass.description: Arrow / dial scenes: label the four compass points N / E / S / W around the rim. Default false. (The rosette uses its landmarks instead.)

person.description: Rosette scene: draw the little person at the centre. Default true.

stem.description: The derived stem sentence — the verbal twin of the figure (a primary convention).

show.description: Show the stem sentence beneath the figure ("A quarter turn clockwise"; on a rosette "Facing the school, turn a quarter turn clockwise to face the park"). Default true. Set false for a clean answer space (the question goes in the block text).

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

draggable.description: Web-only. Pupils drag the end pointer / hand / person round the centre to MAKE the turn; it snaps to the scene's natural positions (a clock hour on the dial, a compass point or landmark elsewhere) and the sweep, the fraction, the degrees and the end heading recompute live. Exploratory — never written back. Default false.
